missions.title: Grammar: I am (identity)
missions.summary: I am [profession / nationality / trait]. One word opens every self-introduction in Spanish.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Soy + [noun/adjective] to express “I am [profession / nationality / trait].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I have
missions.summary: I have / I am [age] years old. Tener expresses possession AND age — two essentials in one verb.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Tengo + [noun] to express “I have / I am [age] years old.”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I like / I love
missions.summary: I like [thing] / I like to [do something]. Gustar works backwards — the thing 'pleases you.' Learn it once, describe everything you enjoy.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Me gusta + [noun / infinitive] to express “I like [thing] / I like to [do something].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I want to
missions.summary: I want to [do something]. Quiero + any verb = any desire. The most natural way to express what you want.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Quiero + [infinitive] to express “I want to [do something].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I have to
missions.summary: I have to / I must [do something]. This single pattern turns every verb you know into an obligation sentence.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Tengo que + [infinitive] to express “I have to / I must [do something].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Going to
missions.summary: I'm going to [do something]. The near-future tense — simpler than the future conjugation and used far more in everyday speech.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Voy a + [infinitive] to express “I'm going to [do something].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I can
missions.summary: I can / I am able to [do something]. Ability, permission, possibility — poder covers all three with one conjugation.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Puedo + [infinitive] to express “I can / I am able to [do something].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Because
missions.summary: ... because [reason]. Porque connects any two ideas with cause and effect.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern [clause] porque [reason] to express “... because [reason].”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: I am (condition or place)
missions.summary: how you are and where you are. Ser is what you are; estar is how and where you are.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Estoy + [adjective/location] to express “how you are and where you are.”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Ser or estar
missions.summary: the same adjective changes meaning with each verb. Es aburrido means he is boring. Está aburrido means he is bored.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern ser vs estar to express “the same adjective changes meaning with each verb.”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: There is / there are
missions.summary: say something exists. One form for singular and plural — hay never changes.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern Hay + [noun] to express “say something exists.”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Present tense
missions.summary: routines and what is happening now. The ending carries the subject, so you can drop the pronoun.
missions.learnerRole: Language learner handling an everyday conversation
objectives: Use the pattern hablo / comes / vive to express “routines and what is happening now.”
Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Negation

Use the pattern naturally in a two-way everyday exchange.
Create a new example rather than only repeating the model sentence.

missions.title: Grammar: Question words
